description: Dead-man for the snapshot-probe watchdog (sensor.camera_health) itself. Its alert automation's four template triggers all read state_attr(...)|int(0), so a dead/unknown sensor - or the script's own error path, which publishes healthy=-1 with zeroed counts - evaluates as 'no fault' on every one of them: the primary liveness monitor could die and be reported as a clean fleet (observed: 10 recorder rows of 'unknown' with all json_attributes wiped). 30 min clears restart windows. RE-ASSERTS hourly (:53) while dead (restart-wipe guard). Added 2026-08-17. (2026-10-10: the unavailable/unknown hold is an OR of single-state conditions with for:, because HA 2026.10 rejects for: with a list of states.) 2026-10-28: START-UP CHECK. A state trigger needs a change after it attaches, so a monitor that was already dead when Home Assistant started (a Core update, or a deploy followed by a restart, that breaks the script) never fired this alert, and the re-assert restores the card without a push. On the start trigger the run now waits up to 30 min for the monitor to be healthy and pages if it is not; its push says the fault has been present since the start, because the check repeats, once per start, a page sent before the restart. The check runs only on a Home Assistant start: an automation reload that re-arms the triggers while the fault is present is not covered. For the -1 error path no other alert pages: that payload keeps a bucketed updated_at, so camera_monitor_stalled stays quiet. An unknown or unavailable sensor (a script that no longer runs at all) stops last_updated, and camera_monitor_stalled pushes that about 60 min after the start (45-min bar plus its 15-min hold).

then.stop: the monitor was healthy at the start or recovered within the hold
